name: Data Flow Diagram (DFD)
definition: A diagram that shows how data moves between external entities, processes and data stores, using circles for processes, open-ended rectangles for data stores, closed rectangles for external entities and labelled curved arrows for data flows.
example: A voting system DFD showing Voters sending their details and vote to the Voting process.

name: Level 0 Data Flow Diagram
definition: An overview (context) data flow diagram that shows the whole system as one process with its external entities, and no data stores or internal processes.
example: A canteen ordering system drawn as one circle between Student and Canteen manager.

name: External Entity
definition: A person, organisation or element outside a system that provides data to it or receives data from it.
example: Students who place orders in a canteen ordering system.

name: Data Store
definition: A place where data is kept between processes, either an electronic file or non-computer storage; drawn as a rectangle open on one side in a DFD.
example: An Electoral roll in a voting system.

name: System Flowchart
definition: A diagram that represents the main processes and devices in a system, using symbols such as online input, direct access storage and cloud, with arrows showing the direction of data.
example: A doctor's system where visit details are entered, stored in a consultation file and sent to the cloud.

name: Decision Tree
definition: A diagram that represents all possible combinations of decisions and their resulting actions, where each path leads to another decision or a final action.
example: A tree that decides whether to buy a car from its mileage, type and colour.

name: Data Dictionary
definition: A comprehensive description of each field in a database, commonly listing the field name, data type, data format, field size, description and an example.
example: UserID: Text, XXXNNNN, size 7, example XYZ1539.

name: Storyboard
definition: A diagram that shows the various interfaces (screens) of a product and the links between them.
example: Three canteen website pages joined by navigation buttons.

name: Network Diagram
definition: A diagram, also called a network map, that documents a network using labelled symbols for the devices (nodes) and lines for how they are connected.
example: A router joined to the internet, two hubs and several labelled computers.

name: Graph and Network Theory
definition: The representation of individuals or categories as nodes and their relationships as links, applied to the design of social networks.
example: A graph of VB's social network with links labelled Friend, Listen and Watch.

name: Gantt Chart
definition: A chart that displays each task of a project on an estimated, dated timeline, showing dependencies, milestones and, where used, resources and percentage complete.
example: A requirements-gathering chart from 30 August to 16 September with a milestone diamond.

name: Process Diary (Log Book)
definition: A record of a project's progress made at regular intervals, including the date, the person, progress, tasks achieved, stumbling blocks, next approaches, reflections and resources used.
example: An entry recording that a price format was fixed and how it was tested.

name: Live Data
definition: Real data from an organisation's actual operation that is used when testing a system.
example: Last term's real canteen orders loaded into a new ordering system.

name: Simulated Data
definition: Data made up by testers to mimic real data or to target particular cases, including boundary and invalid values.
example: A test order with a price of $0.00.

name: Beta Testing
definition: Testing a near-final version of a system with a limited group of real users outside the development team to find remaining faults.
example: Fifty students trial a new school app for a fortnight.

name: Volume Testing
definition: Testing how a system performs with a large amount of data or many users.
example: Loading ten thousand orders to check searches stay fast.

name: Acceptance Testing
definition: Testing in which the client or users check the finished system against agreed criteria to decide whether to accept it.
example: The canteen manager completes her daily tasks and signs off.

name: Normalisation
definition: A relational database design process that minimises data duplication by separating data into smaller linked tables whose fields depend solely on each table's primary key.
example: Moving publisher names out of a Games table into a Publishers table.

name: Schema
definition: A diagram of the organisational structure of a database showing the tables, their fields, the primary keys and the relationships between tables.
example: Games, Publishers and Developers tables joined by one-to-many lines.

name: Foreign Key
definition: A field in one table that holds the primary key value of a record in another table, creating a link between the tables.
example: Publisher_ID in the Games table.

name: Structured Query Language (SQL)
definition: A language used to access and manipulate data in relational databases, using clauses such as SELECT, FROM, WHERE and ORDER BY.
example: SELECT Name FROM Games WHERE Cost > 20 ORDER BY Cost DESC

name: Absolute Reference
definition: A spreadsheet cell reference, written with dollar signs such as $H$1, that does not change when the formula is copied or filled.
example: =D2*$H$1 keeps pointing at the GST rate cell.

name: Pivot Table
definition: A spreadsheet tool that summarises a large table by grouping and totalling its data.
example: Total canteen revenue by item category.

name: Conditional Formatting
definition: A spreadsheet feature that changes how a cell looks automatically when its value meets a rule.
example: Shading a stock cell red when it falls below 10.

name: Bitmap and Vector Graphics
definition: Bitmap images are grids of pixels that blur when enlarged, while vector graphics are built from geometric shapes and stay sharp at any size.
example: A photo is a bitmap; a club logo is best as a vector.
